format.text: Paper A is a three hour exam worth 150 marks, comprised of 150 questions; two-thirds MCQ and one-third EMI. Pass-mark method not stated on that page (links to 'How the written papers are marked'). Revised syllabus reportedly due Jan 2027 (secondary source).

commentary.claim: Psychopharmacology: learn via the receptor rather than lists; exam often asks to explain an adverse effect by the receptor action responsible.
Psychopharmacology: need to distinguish mechanism, adverse effect and interaction.
Neuroscience: need to understand relationships between structures, pathways and function (limbic system, basal ganglia direct/indirect pathways, neurotransmitter systems, neuroplasticity).
Developmental/behavioural topics: identify which model explains a vignette.
Classification/assessment: separate concepts such as obsessions from other preoccupations.
Neuroscience and psychopharmacology carry disproportionate marks relative to how comfortable most trainees feel with them.
